title: Planaria are an example of runaway cellular competency

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planaria are an example of runaway cellular competency

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors propose that planaria exemplify runaway competency: their cells became so good at compensating for structural-gene deficiencies that selection could no longer pick the best genomes, so evolution instead increased generic competency to reach the target morphology, explaining a chaotic genome with robust anatomy.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.4. The Paradox of Robustness: Why the Animal with the Worst Genome Has the Best Anatomy

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We propose that planaria are an example of runaway competency: when cells get really good at making up for deficiencies in the structural genes, evolution has such a hard time selecting for the best genomes that further improvements instead increase generic competency to reach their target morphology despite perturbations.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “4. Discussion › 4.4. The Paradox of Robustness: Why the Animal with the Worst Genome Has the Best Anatomy”. Scope: Planarian flatworms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing comparative data can test some predicted associations. They cannot currently distinguish the proposed historical mechanism from several alternatives, so only parts are resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across planarian lineages, quantify genomic disorder, developmental repair capacity, selection on structural versus regulatory loci, and morphology robustness, then compare predictions of runaway competency with alternative explanations. The hypothesis predicts stronger competency and weaker purifying selection on structural determinants together.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Generic cellular competency has no agreed direct measure.

Available data do not track the proposed ratchet through time.

Historical causation is confounded by asexuality, genome architecture, and population history.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.36
operationalizability: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.28
data adequacy: 0.3
data existence: 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public genomes and regeneration records can reassess the paradoxical pattern the authors want explained. They cannot show that selection shifted onto generic competency because structural defects were hidden. Several non-ratchet histories fit the same present-day facts, so only a proxy pattern is testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare planarian genome disorder and anatomical fidelity with other animals, and ask whether lineages with messier genomes and more regenerative competency show the model's signature of weakened selection on structural genes. The messy-genome plus reliable-anatomy pattern can be checked; the historical claim that competency ran away because selection could not see structural genes cannot.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No dataset records historical selective pressure on planarian structural genes.

Asexuality, abundant stem cells and bioelectric control explain the same pattern without a competency ratchet.
